hypothesis: The best recent candidate used 256 targets per CTA and a 512-source tile. Doubling the source tile to 1024 should halve staging and synchronization rounds for large inputs while preserving one thread per target and the force arithmetic. The four shared arrays require 16,384 bytes, below the 49,152-byte limit; the performance effect remains to be measured.
notes: This is a single 1024-source-tile candidate with a 256-thread block. Recent supplied measurements report correct outcomes for tile 512 (0.00101125 s mean), tile 256 (0.00101702 s), and tile 128 (0.00105828 s). No performance result is available for this candidate; controller correctness and timing determine its outcome.
transformations: Stage source x, y, z, and mass in four 1024-element shared arrays, loading only valid elements of each source tile.
Keep all threads participating in CTA barriers, including target-tail threads; guard force accumulation and output stores with i < n.
Retain self-interaction exclusion and the existing per-interaction force arithmetic.
Use a 256-thread block and 256 items_per_block; static shared memory totals 16,384 bytes.
